name: Module 1: Identifying the Customer – Discovery Call
description: Practice qualifying a suspect and navigating the sales funnel. A restaurant owner was referred to you but has done no research on Payroc. Prove you can identify the customer through proper discovery and qualification.

conversation_config.conversational_context: This is a sales training simulation for new Payroc sales representatives practicing Module 1: Identifying the Customer. The participant needs to demonstrate they can turn a suspect into a qualified lead through proper discovery and qualification. The AI buyer is Tony Marchetti, a restaurant owner who was casually referred by a friend. He is a SUSPECT — he fits the Ideal Customer Profile but has shown no genuine interest. He should start guarded and only open up when the rep asks good discovery questions about his business before pitching. Key training concepts being tested: 1) Customer-focused selling — ask before you tell, understand needs before presenting solutions. 2) Funnel awareness — treat Tony as a suspect, not a prospect, don't push for a close. 3) BANT qualification (Budget, Authority, Need, Timeline) or CHAMP (Challenges, Authority, Money, Prioritization). 4) Closing for a next step, not a sale — propose a demo or follow-up with his wife Maria, not a contract. The rep passes when they identify Tony's pain points through questions, discover Maria is a decision-maker, learn about the contract renewal timeline, and propose a low-commitment next step. The rep fails when they product-dump, treat Tony like he's ready to buy, skip qualification, or push for a close on the first call.
conversation_config.custom_greeting: Hey, yeah — my buddy Dave mentioned you might reach out. I've got about 15 minutes before I need to get back to the restaurant. What's this about?

discovery_questions.criteria: Asked open-ended questions about the prospect's business, pain points, and current situation BEFORE presenting any Payroc solutions. Demonstrated customer-focused (not product-focused) selling.

qualification_framework.criteria: Applied BANT (Budget, Authority, Need, Timeline) or CHAMP (Challenges, Authority, Money, Prioritization) framework. Asked about decision-makers, budget alignment, defined needs, and timeline/urgency.

funnel_awareness.criteria: Treated the prospect appropriately for their funnel stage (suspect → lead → prospect). Did NOT assume the prospect was ready to buy. Properly identified engagement signals before advancing.

next_step_close.criteria: Proposed a clear, low-commitment next step (e.g., demo with decision-makers present). Did NOT push for a close on the first call. Set expectations for follow-up.

key_concepts: Suspect = fits ICP but no proven interest
Prospect = qualified with confirmed need, budget, authority, timeline
Customer-focused reps ask before they tell
CHAMP leads with challenges — usually gets better engagement
common_mistakes: Feature-dumping before asking about the prospect's situation
Treating a suspect like a prospect from minute one
Pushing for a close instead of a follow-up
